newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close up on harvest delay prospects.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close up on harvest delay prospects.

text.p: Forecasts for wet weather this week in the U.S. Midwest, which would delay soybean harvest and slow maturation of the soy crop, boosted CBOT soybean futures to a higher close, traders said.
"The fact is it's a Catch 22. The clouds are keeping frost away but the clouds are dropping rain," a trader said.

News Taiwan bought U.S. soybeans also contributed to the advances, they said. "It was up on talk of harvest delays and postponement of maturity," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co. "On the demand side Taiwan bought 162,000 (tonnes) soy and 54,000 (tonnes) of corn last night."
Commercial bull spreading and firm soybean basis markets contributed support, they said.
"There was a lot of commercial bull spreading in beans and obviously weather is a factor. The cif is strong and again it's a function of weather being too wet," a trader said.
Meteorologists early Wednesday said widespread rain was forecast for the U.S. Central Plains and Midwest for the balance of the week.
Soybeans closed 1/2 to 4-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with November up 4-1/2 at $7.95-3/4 cents per bushel and January closed up 3-3/4 cents at $8.02.

November soybeans touched a session high of $7.97 per bushel. Technicians early Wednesday cited the $7.95 per bushel mark as initial chart resistance with the next resistance level at roughly $8.02-1/2.

Cargill Inc bought two million bushels of March and roughly one half million November and May, the traders said. Refco Inc and Smith Barney each bought two million November and Tenco Inc bull spread two million November/January at 6-1/4 cents, they said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 44,000 contracts, down from 51,497 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Lee B. Stern and Co bought 600 January $8.50 calls at 14 to 14-1/2 cents, Cargill Investor Services sold 300 January $8.00 calls at 15 to 15-1/4 cents and sold 300 November $8.00 puts at 21 cents, traders said.
Options volume was estimated at 13,500, down from 18,242 Tuesday.
